question: In the review of lithium-mediated ammonia electrosynthesis, what ammonia faradaic efficiency did LiTFSI give in the gas diffusion electrode flow electrolyser with a PtAu anode?
rendered:
[Pathways to sustainable lithium-mediated ammonia electrosynthesis: tuning reaction environment and advancing reactor design, page 11]
RSC Advances Review Fig. 4 Evolution of reactor design for Li-NRR. (a) Batch (one-compartment) cell.51 Copyright 2025, Springer Nature; (b) continuous ﬂow cell with gas diﬀusion electrodes.12 Copyright 2023, Springer Nature; (c) proton conducting membrane (membrane electrode assembly) reactor.54 Copyright 2024, Springer Nature. To resolve the instability of conventional platinum anodes in organic media within previous systems,26,42 Fu et al. advanced the GDE ow cell concept for NH3 electrosynthesis by coupling the Li-NRR with HOR occurring on a platinum–gold (PtAu) coated anode.12 This catalytic improvement signicantly lowered the anode potential (∼0.6 V vs. Pt), eﬀectively preventing the oxidative decomposition and polymerization of the THF solvent typically triggered at higher potentials of the Pt anode. The GDE system with LiBF4/THF solution achieved a faradaic eﬃciency of 61 ± 1% and an energy eﬃciency of 13 ± 1% at 1 bar, representing a major step toward sustainable ammonia electrosynthesis under ambient conditions. Interestingly, by using this GDE ow electrolyser to examine the eﬀects of diﬀerent electrolytes on Li-NRR performance, they revealed that LiTFSI, while demonstrating high-performance in batch systems, consistently showed poor ammonia FE (18%) because sulfur-based decomposition products poisoned the PtAu HOR catalyst.56 By contrast, LiBF4 still demonstrated the highest performance
